assessment: Owner START runs migration before interrupted-job replay, readiness, private-intent replay, desired drain, and new save acceptance. Unknown ledger schema, unknown migration marker, and failed migration transactions leave the new-write gate closed.

Previously upgraded public-v1 databases are detected from unmigrated rows. Disabled or root-mismatched sources, corrupt/missing/changed files, cancelled jobs, and fresh uncertain heartbeats receive durable blocked decisions; the count remains visible after restart.

The newest verifiable old job wins per document. Equal-time same-content ambiguity and a newer uncertain fresh indexing claim block promotion for that document. Completed old jobs remain history only.

Decision markers, new desired revision/job, and old-row history status commit in one SQLite transaction. Injected marker failure rolls back the new job and leaves START and write ACK closed; replay converges to one eligible new job.

A later valid save on a document with a blocked legacy indexing row creates a claimable and completable new desired job while retaining the old row and diagnostic. Active-job predicates exclude only rows carrying a blocked legacy migration marker; an unmarked live modern claim remains fenced.

Source and document identity, metadata, alias, and saved file are retained. Hash-only aliases keep null lexical and canonical origins. No journal deletion, inferred origin path, or automatic full rebuild was found.
